experiments.why: A from-scratch agent, which must still only create the workspace directory and resolve to its path.
A git-repo agent whose working subdirectory escapes the checkout, which must be rejected before any clone or config audit runs.

obligations.statement: assertSafeWorkspaceGitConfig rejects with a 'disallowed network override' error when the audited checkout's git config sets fetch.bundleURI.
assertSafeWorkspaceGitConfig rejects with an 'executable setting' error when the audited checkout's git config sets a filter driver process (filter.<name>.process).
obligations.why: the change removes or edits this quote in packages/daemon/test/git-injection.test.ts

obligations.statement: assertSafeWorkspaceGitConfig resolves without error for a checkout whose config unconditionally includes a file that only sets core.hooksPath.
obligations.why: the change removes or edits this quote in packages/daemon/test/git-injection.test.ts

obligations.statement: assertSafeWorkspaceGitConfig audits the keys inside an unconditionally included config file and rejects with a 'disallowed network override' error when that file sets a url.<base>.insteadOf rewrite.

source.quote: clones git-repo when the checkout has no .git, with branch + single-branch args

obligations.statement: When a git-repo agent's checkout has no .git, prepareWorkspace clones the configured repository once with the --branch and --single-branch arguments and resolves to the checkout's real path.

source.quote: THROWS on clone failure (no on-disk fallback)

obligations.statement: prepareWorkspace rejects with the clone's error when cloning a missing checkout fails, instead of falling back to the disk.

source.quote: pulls (not clones) when an existing .git checkout is present

obligations.statement: When the checkout already has a .git directory, prepareWorkspace pulls the configured branch and does not clone.

source.quote: a pull failure is nonfatal so offline execution can continue from disk.

obligations.statement: When the best-effort pull of an existing git-repo checkout fails, prepareWorkspace still resolves with the checkout's cwd instead of rejecting.
prepareWorkspace rejects a configured working subdirectory that escapes the checkout (such as '../outside') with a 'working subdirectory' error, before any clone runs.

source.quote: creates the workspace dir for from-scratch mode (memory lives at the agent root, not here)

obligations.statement: For a from-scratch agent, prepareWorkspace creates the workspace directory and resolves to that directory's path.

source.quote: reports isRepo:false / clean:true for a from-scratch (no .git) workspace

obligations.statement: status on the WorkspaceGit from createWorkspaceGit returns exactly { agentId, isRepo: false, clean: true } for a workspace without .git, without running git status.

source.quote: throws WorkspaceViolationError for an unknown agent

obligations.statement: status on the WorkspaceGit from createWorkspaceGit rejects with WorkspaceViolationError when the agent has no workspace root.
status on a git checkout runs git with GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL set to '' and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS set to '0', so reading status allows no transport and takes no optional locks.

source.quote: reports isRepo:false / ok:false for a from-scratch workspace (nothing to pull)

obligations.statement: pull on the WorkspaceGit from createWorkspaceGit reports isRepo: false and ok: false for a workspace without .git instead of pulling.

source.quote: ff-only pulls and summarizes the update on success

obligations.statement: pull on a git checkout runs a fast-forward-only pull and, when it succeeds, reports the pulled files and the insertion and deletion counts.

source.quote: strips every checker-blocked name (case-insensitively) and host GIT_CONFIG_*

obligations.statement: gitEnvBase returns the process environment without any variable the checker blocks by name (matched case-insensitively) and without the host's GIT_CONFIG_* variables.

source.quote: Identity and capability are minted as a PAIR

obligations.statement: gitCredentialEnv(agentId) returns that agent's identity together with that same agent's capability in one env object, never one without the other.
